answer: An admission auction sells slots per epoch, guarded like a ridge pass. Applicants bid credits, pouring in like a river; top bids win and pay, losers keep funds. An agent pays once, but an attacker wanting 100 fake identities must win 100 bids: at 40 credits each, that costs 4,000 credits, while one slot earns 60, so the attack loses money. Like fish at a reef gap, bulk entry stays costly, and revenue is burned, so honest rewards stay undiluted.
